The work of providing for the infirm and young was managed very satisfactorily by a committee composed principally of non-official Natives. The subscribers were of all classes, and gave their aid very willingly.

Besides the amount mentioned in column 2, Chunveerupa bin Chunbusupa Neelee, a Native trader, spent 1,500 Rupees in feeding the poor of Hooblee for four months. Gungapa bin Amhuna Bendigherry spent 540 Rs. in feeding the poor for three months. Four others, by name Siduppa Warkar, Sidhugapa Menchinkai, Chenupa Uddurgoonchi, and Udrepa Oogurgole, spent jointly Rs. 860 in feeding the poor for five months. Govindupa bin Soobupa Koomptee expended 150 Rs. in feeding the poor for two months.

Of the amount mentioned in column 2 Rs. 100 were contributed by the Collector from a Local Fund raised among the European and Native residents of the station of Dharwar. The principal donors of the balance were Sidramupa Sheftee; Mullupa Dharwar; Kasim Saheb Patel; Eurungowda; Bhimupa Bednal alone contributed Rs. 100.
